# clickhouse_clickstack_app (Resource)

Manages a ClickStack app: a single-file React (TSX) application that ClickStack renders in a sandbox on top of the team's data. Every change to `code` or `purpose` saves a new version, kept in the app's version history; edits made in the app builder show up as drift and are overwritten on the next apply. Requires Apps to be enabled for the team.

~> **Note:** This resource is in beta and its behavior may change in future provider versions. It is built on the ClickStack Apps API, which is in preview.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An app whose TSX source lives next to the configuration as a plain App.tsx.
# Apps can't take parameters, so values such as source ids go into the code:
# App.tsx holds one '__CONFIG__' placeholder, and replace() swaps in every value
# at once as a jsonencode()d object. jsonencode() quotes and escapes strings
# (so a value like "Bob's errors" is safe) and keeps numbers and booleans as
# they are. The file stays valid TSX that editors and linters understand.
resource "clickhouse_clickstack_app" "checkout_errors" {
  name    = "Checkout errors"
  purpose = "Shows checkout errors by service for on-call engineers."
  code = replace(file("${path.module}/App.tsx"), "'__CONFIG__'", jsonencode({
    sourceId = clickhouse_clickstack_source.logs.id
    heading  = "Bob's checkout errors"
  }))

  # Defaults to true. A private app is visible only to the API key's user.
  is_shared = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `code` (String) The app's TSX source, up to 500000 characters. It must default-export a React component and import only modules the app runtime provides (such as `@hdx/app`). Typically read with `file()`. To pass in values such as source IDs, put one quoted placeholder in the code and swap it with `replace()` for a `jsonencode()`d object, as in the example: strings are quoted and escaped, other types keep their type, and the file stays valid TSX, unlike with `templatefile()`, which clashes with JavaScript's `${...}` syntax.
- `name` (String) App name, 1 to 60 characters, without leading or trailing whitespace.

### Optional

- `is_shared` (Boolean) Whether the whole team can see and edit the app. Defaults to `true`. When `false`, only the app's creator — the user the API key belongs to — can see it. Only the creator can change this, so a plan that flips it with a different API key fails. On ClickHouse Cloud an API key is not a user anyone signs in as, so a private app is visible to no one in the UI.
- `purpose` (String) What the app is for, who it helps, and how to use it, up to 2000 characters. Shown on the app's About page and used as context when the app is edited in the app builder. Defaults to empty.
- `team` (String) Team ID to manage this app under (`x-hdx-team`). Self-hosted only. Changing this forces the app to be replaced.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the app.
- `version_id` (String) ID of the app's current version. Changes whenever `code` or `purpose` changes, so it can be used to trigger dependent resources.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Apps can be imported by their ID.
terraform import clickhouse_clickstack_app.checkout_errors 507f1f77bcf86cd799439011

# For an app in a non-default team (multi-team / EE deployments), prefix the ID
# with the team ID:
terraform import clickhouse_clickstack_app.checkout_errors 65f0c0ffeecafef00dba5e01/507f1f77bcf86cd799439011

# To find the ID, list the apps the API key can see. The response is an
# envelope of the form {"data": [{"id": "...", "name": "...", ...}], "meta": {...}}.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLICKSTACK_API_KEY" \
  "$CLICKSTACK_ENDPOINT/api/v2/apps" | jq -r '.data[] | "\(.id)\t\(.name)"'
```
